title: Overdrive live coach: a cue
description: The data of a `cue` event on GET /v1/live/sessions/{id}/cues (Server-Sent Events, spec §12.1, ADR 0038): one spoken line, ready to play. id is the cue's number in the session from 1; it is also the event's SSE id, so the app resumes with Last-Event-ID, and it names the cue in POST /v1/live/sessions/{id}/cues/{cueId}/played. text is what is said, 1 to 80 characters, shown on the plate under the overlay. trigger says why it was made: step-start, two-minutes, power-drift, cadence-sag, heart-rate-climb, strong-finish (a model wrote the line) or must-say (the agent's own words); a reader must treat a name it does not know as a plain string. audio is the speech itself, inline: format (mp3 unless the owner chose another) and the bytes in base64 (a cue of 80 characters is about 60 KB, 80 KB as base64; at most 400000 bytes). It is inline, not a link, because it makes one request instead of two on a flaky connection, needs no second authentication, no cache and no clean-up on the service, and the audio is never kept. createdAt is when the cue was ready (UTC); expiresAt is when it stops being worth playing (UTC): a cue that arrives after it (a stream that came back) is not played. ttlMs is expiresAt minus createdAt in milliseconds, for an app that does not trust its clock: it plays a cue only within ttlMs of receiving it.
